note: Boulders (Dave 2026-10-21): not rocks; a pick (or an axe, half as fast) breaks them into rough stones. The yield is plain math from the size: volume (an ellipsoid of the boulder's radius and height_ratio x radius high, the buried part included) x density x yield, divided by the mass of one stone (weights.json, 1 kg), is the number of stones; a 1 m radius boulder makes about 4600, 0.3 m about 125, 1.2 m about 7900 at yield 0.5. STONES PER BLOW (tools; Dave 12 Nov 2026, TEST-013: "a stone pickaxe ... at least 1 rock per swing and higher tiers more rocks per swing ... destroy the rock faster and still get the same amount of rock while degrading the durability less for higher tiers") are by the tool class and material (items.json) of the tool IN HAND, which must be on the hotbar: pick stone 1, bronze 2, iron 3, steel 4. 14 Nov 2026 (GOALS-REPAIR R2b): copper pick 1.5 and copper axe 0.75, between stone and bronze, PROVISIONAL (GOALS-REPAIR A-14). A fraction carries over between blows (the boulder's progress). Every blow wears the tool once (drops.json tool_wear rock), so a better pick wears less for the same stone. An axe is the wrong tool: half the pick's stones of its material, and tool_wear rock wears it 5 per blow. The stones in a boulder are fixed by its size whatever the tool. Each piece rolls its own luck double, ore and flint. The boulder shrinks as stones come out (cube root of what is left) and is gone with the last one; what is left is saved (world_items.json boulders). Every blow wears the tool like other work (durability in items.json, drops.json tool_wear per_use may add more). Boulders are server-owned and laid out like loose stones: per 32 m cell, up to max_per_cell, only where the ground rises more than min_slope or at a water bank, deterministic from the cell. size: radius_min..radius_max, radius_power > 1 makes small ones commoner. luck_extra: the chance that a blow's stone comes away as two (and takes two from the boulder), passed through the luck function (0 switches it off; 0.05 means about 5 percent at luck 0, about 7 percent at +10, 3.5 percent at -10).

ore.note: Ore and coal from boulders (guide finding F-23, FLINT_ORE_SPEC.md): a boulder that lies within reach_m of an ore body of the terrain (the geology's ore_bodies) is an outcrop with that ore with chance boulder_share (decided from the boulder's key, so it is the same every time). A PICK (not an axe) takes the ore: each piece that comes away is the ore with chance piece_share, else stone. Iron needs no better pick than copper: there is no bronze pick in the game, and an iron pick needs iron ore first (a circle), so the ladder is made by rarity, not by tool. items: ore name in data/tables/resources.json -> item id. 2026-10-31 (Sal): `needs_material` lists which pick materials may take each ore (14 Nov 2026, GOALS-REPAIR R2b: a Copper pick takes what a stone one does, not iron; master s2 "Bronze mines Iron"): coal, copper and tin with any pick, iron only with a bronze, iron or steel pick, so the ladder is stone pick (copper, tin, coal) -> forge -> bronze ingot -> bronze pickaxe -> iron. The server reads needs_material in _hit_boulder (checked 3 Nov 2026), so a stone pick cannot take iron. 2026-11-10 (Steve, Jamie's tin check): a compact ore body (lens, halo, pipe, vein, placer) within reach_m comes first, the nearest of them; else a coal seam or other layer of the province under the boulder counts only where one of its bands lies within layer_depth_m under the bedrock surface. Bodies of ores not in items (gems, flint) are skipped instead of hiding the rest. 10 Nov 2026 (coordinator, item_system.md): rock salt. An evaporite salt bed (a layer) shows in boulders where its band comes within layer_depth_m of the bedrock surface, and a salt dome (a pipe) only where its top does; its pieces are the same Salt as sea salt, with any pick. 10 Nov 2026 (Steve, Dave's seven building tiers: Concrete = Lime powder + Sand + Stone): a boulder that is not an ore outcrop is of its own bedrock (TileTerrainData.bedrock_name_at, the layered rock at the bedrock surface under it). Over a rock in `rocks` (rock name -> item) a share rock_boulder_share of the boulders (from the key) give that item: each piece a pick takes is it with chance rock_piece_share, else stone; any pick material. Limestone, chalk and marble all give Limestone.
ore.hammer_note: Dave 15 Nov 2026 (TREE_WOOD_TOOLS_DESIGN.md s1, W-12): the Stone Hammer breaks rock and takes copper, tin, coal, salt and limestone like a stone pick; iron ore still needs a bronze or better PICK (pick_only). A Wooden hammer does not break rock (no tools.hammer.wood rate).

copper_rocks.note: Copper rocks (Dave 16 Nov 2026, his photo of real copper ore: rough rocks wholly coated in green to blue-green malachite, fist size to boulders; "they should come in various sizes that have various amounts of copper in them. they should be strewn about the lands a bit and more abundant along river beds and shores. larger boulders should happen near the base of mountains some times."). Server rows like boulders with ore copper, mined the same way (a pick or the Stone Hammer, any material). Per 32 m cell: `tries` spots; a spot takes a rock with chance `chance` anywhere on land, or with chance `water_chance` when it lies in water no deeper than bed_depth_m (a river or lake bed) or on a dry bank within bank_reach_m of water; never in deeper water. Size radius_min..radius_max (radius_power > 1: small ones commoner). One more try per cell is the mountain-foot boulder: with chance foot.chance, on gentle ground (rise per metre under max_slope) where the ground climbs more than rise_m within reach_m (at most 26 m: the scatter reads no ground past its prefetched pad). grade_min..grade_max (from the rock's key): the share of its pieces that are copper ore, so the copper in a rock is its size times its grade; every copper outcrop boulder of the geology gets a grade too, in place of ore piece_share. A share hand_share of the sizes (Dave 17 Nov 2026: "smaller rocks can be picked by hand and the larger rocks should be harvested with a hammer") is a loose Copper ore picked up by hand instead of a rock to break; slot: the cell's slots from 8. 17 Nov 2026 (Dave: "near rivers and mountains. strick rules"; keep some land scatter; copper and tin rocks "anywhere from .5m to 2m in size ... for both of them"): rocks to break radius 0.25..1.0 (the geology outcrops clamped too), a share hand_share of the sizes is a loose piece instead; banks 10 m, 6 tries at 70%; mountain foot 25%. All values PROVISIONAL, docs/design/COPPER_ROCKS.md For Dave CR-1..CR-10.

tin_rocks.note: Tin rocks (Dave 17 Nov 2026, his photo of cassiterite: pale speckled granite with white quartz veins carrying dark brown-black crystals, a crusted chunk, and smooth dark water-worn pebbles; "it is found along riverbeds often smaller the further down stream you go and the closer to the mountains it should be in bolder sizes and can be harvested by hammer. the smaller rocks should be picked by hand."). Laid out like copper_rocks (server_items._lay_out_ore_rocks) but only in shallow water and on banks, and only within near_body_m of a tin body of the geology (its river placers). Size from the relief: how far the ground climbs within relief_reach_m (steep valley sides near the mountains = boulders, flat ground far downstream = pebbles): radius = radius_min..radius_max x relief / relief_full_m, half of it jittered. Under hand_share of the size range it is a loose Tin ore picked up by hand; bigger is a boulder row broken with a hammer (or a pick). grade_min..grade_max: share of a boulder's pieces that are Tin ore. Slots 16..23 of the cell. All PROVISIONAL, docs/design/COPPER_ROCKS.md For Dave TN-1..TN-6.

flint.note: Flint (guide finding F-02, FLINT_ORE_SPEC.md): each stone that comes off a boulder is a flint nodule instead with this chance, more near water. Bank stones (drops.json ground_scatter.bank.flint) are flint with their own chance. Flint makes the hide scraper, javelin and sickle.
